name: certainty
description: Having strong trust in an explanation or prediction based on evidence and/or reasoning.
perceptions: I trust this explanation or prediction.
My reasons to trust it are based on experience or logic.
examples: She's never late -- she'll be here.
The deer will eat our shrubs this winter.

guidance.description: 6 steps to creating certainty in uncertain times

After decades of getting people to trust their gut, build confidence in themselves, and stand up for what they think, the world of psychology has a new message: Don’t Be So Sure. In fact, the more certain you are, the less likely it is that you’re correct.
Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder thrives on doubt, making the search for certainty a never-ending cycle.

variations.name: certainty of memory
variations.description: Solid trust in your memory that something happened in the past.

guidance.description: Most of the time, most of us can trust our memories. It may help to be aware that false memories are a thing.

examples: Yes, I closed the garage door.

comparisons.description: Faith is a form of certainty based on belief rather than experience or logic.

Certainty is not necessarily about positive things. For example, you could be certain that the volcano will destroy the town someday. An optimist would focus on the best outcomes within that certain scenario, for example that there's enough warning to evacuate the people.

To be certain of something, you are trusting two things: the underlying patterns and your interpretation of those patterns for this particular scenario. If you don't trust a pattern, that's called 'doubt'. If you don't trust how you're applying a pattern, that's 'uncertainty'. e.g. Whether or not you doubt natural selection, you can still be uncertain about how a bacterial sample will evolve over 1,000 generations.

commentaries.quote: The longing for certainty...is in every human mind. But certainty is generally illusion.
Here's the story that many of us inhabit: life is dangerous. Survival requires control. Control requires certainty. Certainty requires simplicity. Complexity and doubt are dangerous.

When we personalize outcomes, our ego conflates being certain with being right. We then filter out ideas that question our desired outcome, ignore feedback we do not wish to hear, or deny data that 'gets in our way' that we do not wish to see.
